title: Dink Johnson and Ernest Johnson (Nene) in Los Angeles
summary: Discussion of Dink Johnson and the drummer Ernest Johnson, who Williams says changed his name out West, and what they played.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Well, I think, did you ever meet Dink Johnson, a drummer and a piano player?
Yeah, oh yeah, I met Dink. Oh yes, indeed. What become of him?

He died in 1954, I believe, up in Portland at his brother's place. I made some records of him about 15 years ago. What was his brother's name now? I can't remember, it was Bill Johnson, the namesplayer. Bill Johnson, I believe. This is another brother, I can't think of his name now.
Yeah, that's the one I knew, Bill Johnson. They had another brother.

Yeah, and there was another one that played guitar or something. That's right, that's right. But I only met Bill and the Dink. And Dink. Dink died just in 54. Yeah. Was he old? Born in 92, so he was eight years older than you.
Yeah, that's the name. He was about 62 when he died. Yeah, they tell me he's a New Orleans boy from across the lake.

He's sliding out. Yeah, he's all over in there somewhere. Maybe Biloxi, I'm not sure. Bill Ford along in there. Yeah, that's what I heard from over the lake. Uh-huh. He says he told everybody he was born in New Orleans, but he was just near here.

No, over the lake. It wasn't good in here. No, it wasn't here, no, over the lake, because I didn't know him. First time I... Did he ever play with you out there? No, he never did play. We'd seen him play with someone else.
Yeah. I think he played the Black and Pan band. Did you hear them? Yeah, Ernest Johnson. Was that, um, the name of Southern? I can't think of his name. That's right, Harry Southern.

He's a trombone player. That was the leader. That was the trombone player. He was a leader. Ernest Johnson was with them? Yeah, Ernest Johnson. We call him Nene. Bright fella. What did he play? Something. That's Ernest... That's, that's Peele's brother. You heard of Lil' Peele? Yeah, and that's... Well, that's his brother. Nene. Nene, yeah, yeah. Nene Poico. Poico is his real name. That's right, that's right, that's right. Ernest Johnson is Dr. Ernest. But he changed... No, no, he changed his name out there. Yeah. Oh, sure, he changed his name. Changed his name to Johnson. So Poico. Yeah, sure, that was such a funny name, you know. Yeah. Yeah, he's a garra.

He's not there, he is. If I remember rightly, Dink told me that they used to tell him that he was their brother or cousin or something sometimes. Did he? Did he? Yeah. He wasn't related at all, but they'd tell people that. Sometime, you know, I don't know why. Yeah, I guess so.
Well, didn't he play with the superior? That's what Lawrence Morrero told me. Who, Dink?

Ernest Johnson, Ernest Cuoco, Nene. Well, I don't know. That might have been for my time. Yeah, well, that's what he said. He played with him. He played with him. Well, I went out in Los Angeles, I found him out there. Oh, yeah. Yeah, I found him. He had been out there a long time.

He played with that piano player, Sonny Clay, huh, too, out there. Sonny Clay? You know him? No, I don't know. He was a drummer and a piano player. No, Sonny Clay. I guess he came late on that, but Cuoco recorded on Coronet with him. Oh, I see.
